_doc.description: Homepage-only slice of The T content. Rendered by src/web/features/theT/components/TheTHome.tsx. Field names mirror the canonical Static Upload Tubi Blog data — `eyebrow`, `subtitle`, `categoryTag`, `genreTag`, `watchLink`, etc. — so this file can be regenerated from the source JSONs without renaming. Section chrome (`{section}.header.title` + `{section}.header.subtitle`) is editorial copy authored alongside the slot data so the same JSON drives both the section heading and its content.
_doc.source: Article slots: ~/Desktop/Static Upload Tubi Blog/{listicles,single-titles,world-cup}.json. Watchlist rail: ~/Desktop/Watchlist/watchlist.json (`home` section), with poster art mirrored into `static/blog/the-t/watchlist/home_{1..6}_poster.jpg`.
_doc.doNotInclude: intro, items[], cast[], whatsComing[], full keepReading[] — only the fields the homepage actually renders should ship in this chunk.
_doc.linking: Every article card / hero uses the canonical URL `/the-t/articles/<slug>`. Each slot stores just the bare `slug` (e.g. `best-anime-on-tubi`); the renderer (`homePageData.ts → buildArticleHref`) prepends the prefix. The article route (`containers/Article.tsx`) fetches the matching JSON under `static/blog/the-t/data/articles/` and branches on its `type` field (`'article'` vs `'listicle'`) to dispatch to ArticleDetailsPage (single) or ArticleListPage (listicle), so the article kind is NOT duplicated here. The optional `watchLink` on some slots is reserved for CTAs that bypass the article and route straight into the Tubi catalog (e.g. the Watchlist row → catalog title); it does NOT influence the article href.
